title: Supplier Lead Time Analysis
description: Analyze purchase order lead times by supplier. For each supplier, compute the **average lead time** (days from order to receipt), **maximum lead time**, **minimum lead time**, and **order count**. Order by average lead time descending to identify slowest suppliers.
solution_sql: SELECT supplier_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, ROUND(AVG(received_date - ordered_date), 1) AS avg_lead_time_days, MAX(received_date - ordered_date) AS max_lead_time_days, MIN(received_date - ordered_date) AS min_lead_time_days FROM purchase_orders GROUP BY supplier_id ORDER BY avg_lead_time_days DESC

test_cases.description: 4 suppliers: S4 avg=14.5d (slowest), S2 avg=8.7d, S1 avg=7.3d, S3 avg=6.0d (fastest)

hints: Subtract ordered_date from received_date to compute lead time in days — PostgreSQL date subtraction returns an integer.
Group by supplier_id and apply AVG, MAX, MIN to the lead time expression within the aggregation.
explanation: Lead time = received_date - ordered_date. Supplier 4: 14 days (Jan 10→24) and 15 days (Feb 5→20) → avg=14.5 (slowest). Supplier 2: 7, 11, 8 days → avg=8.7. Supplier 1: 7, 7, 8 days → avg=7.3. Supplier 3: 7, 5 days → avg=6.0 (fastest). This analysis identifies suppliers causing delays and informs SLA negotiations.
